glosses: to deafen, to soundproof (to make something soundproof)

examples.text: La moquette permet d’insonoriser les bruits de pas.

glosses: Augmenter l'étanchéité sonore d'un matériau, d'un espace.

examples.text: On va insonoriser vos fenêtres : vous n'entendrez plus les bruits de la rue.
The contestant was placed in a soundproof booth so he could not receive help from the audience.

The electrical activity of the subject's cerebral cortex was recorded in a state of relative rest, after a 5 min adaptation of the subject to a dark soundproof chamber. The biopotentials were recorded from the electroencephaloscope screen […]

glosses: To make resistant to transmitting sound.

examples.text: We soundproofed the room so we couldn't hear the road noises; unfortunately we couldn't hear the fire alarm either.
It almost goes without saying that the train is fully soundproofed, with double-glazed windows and highly efficient air-conditioning by the British firm of J. Stone.
Soundproofing a room may be as simple as sealing gaps around a door, or it may require rebuilding an entire wall or lowering a ceiling.

glosses: rendere impenetrabile o meno penetrabile ai rumori mediante particolari accorgimenti
